highlighted_spans: The paper reports a heterozygous LDLR c.1879G>A (p.A627T) variant identified in 7 affected family members with elevated LDL-C and clinical features of familial hypercholesterolemia. The study describes the variant's association with the disease phenotype but does not present any functional assay data (e.g., protein expression, receptor activity, trafficking) to directly assess the variant's molecular impact.
